minor: Consumer gap, E versus F. All SA anchors are B(E) norms, as the note states in Section 6. The packet's upper-cameron-compactness C3 and raw-block tuple norms are K(F) Holder norms with constant columns, and e0 is not in E. A radius-small F-norm version of (20) should not be expected. The constant column gives a first-chaos variance over about R^d spaced translated test vectors, which is reviewer reasoning and gives ||driver e_disp||_E of order R^(d/2) in L2. At R_delta this would scale like delta^((1-a-d)/2), which diverges. A successor therefore must not place (20) directly into the F tuple norm. It must use an E-based route, for example a localized initial cutoff with its own polynomial budget, or prove a separate F bound. This does not affect SA1-SA3. The phrase 'the missing EXPECTED norm anchor' should be read as restricted to E.

Lines 281-282 refer to 'the infinite-spatial-rank projection from the separate accepted Cameron estimate'. In the packet's upper-cameron-compactness note, P_J is a finite-rank projection, and its Section 9 refutes uniform-R tails for fixed J. Any uniform-R U note is not in this packet, so this description and the space of its Cameron budget are unverified here. The mathematics of (20) does not depend on this, because it covers every deterministic Pi.

Section 6 proves an expected norm at R_delta but does not prove that R_delta=1/delta+2 covers any consumer cone or supplies any mask-removal comparison. The note makes no such claim, and a consumer must prove it separately.

Notation is overloaded: zeta is both the base mask and the exponent at line 276, and Q is both the Schatten index and the cube Q_L. Renaming the exponent would aid later reuse. There is no mathematical ambiguity in context.
The stated range q>=1 in (3) and Q>=2 is broader than what is effective. gamma<1/2 and d>=1 force q*gamma>d only when q>2d, so q>2 always. This is harmless and consistent with the no-HS boundary.
The C_(Q,B) constants also depend on the fixed auxiliary profiles chi0 and psi0 chosen in Section 2. This is covered by 'all fixed parameters' but is not displayed in the subscript.
